items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google The Washington Capitals have a new player of the game award, and it’s a vintage piece of equipment with special significance. Future Washington Capitals captain Tom Wilson revealed the special item after the Capitals defeated the New Jersey Devils 4-2 in a Saturday matinee at Capital One Arena. “I think we’re going with ‘Legend of the Game,'” Wilson said, sliding out an Alex Ovechkin rookie-era helmet from his Bauer bag. “We can only start with one guy. Our leader.” Wilson then handed Ovechkin his old bucket, which he briefly affixed on his head. “I’m still young, by the way,” Ovechkin said. “All right, guys. I think today, great job [like] Carbs said, ’40 hard minutes.’ LT, great job, but Vincent.” (Ovechkin pronounced Vincent in a heavy French accent.) Desharnais then threw on the helmet before dropping some of Ovechkin’s rookie vernacular. “Sick,” he said as the team laughed. “Stay f***ing hot, boys. Let’s f***ing keep going.” Monumental Sports Network host Tarik El-Bashir reported that the idea was Wilson’s alone. Ovechkin first wore the mirrored tinted visor, which gave the young Russian superstar a distinctive, RoboCop-like appearance, 21 years ago during his debut season in the NHL, and it caused controversy. Devils goaltender Martin Brodeur complained that it gave Ovechkin an unfair advantage because opponents couldn’t see his eyes. NHL general managers later voted 29–1 against allowing mirrored visors in 2006, with Washington’s George McPhee as the lone dissenter, though the prohibition was never formally written into the rulebook. Ovechkin reluctantly switched to a smoky-tinted visor, but nearly two decades later, he still considers the original his favorite.

items.title: Panthers Recall Cole Reinhardt
items.summary: The Florida Panthers have recalled winger Cole Reinhardt from AHL Charlotte.
items.body: Register Login Panthers Recall Cole Reinhardt By Brian La Rose | at October 17, 2026 3:30 pm With no extra healthy players on their roster heading into tonight’s game against Seattle, the Panthers have elected to give themselves a bit more depth. The team announced that they’ve recalled winger Cole Reinhardt from AHL Charlotte. The 26-year-old played in 59 games last season between Vegas and Florida, who claimed him off waivers a little before the trade deadline to give themselves another healthy body down the stretch. Between the two teams, he notched nine goals and six assists along with 129 hits in 10:39 per night of playing time. But more than half of his offense came in his limited time with the Panthers as he potted six goals with two helpers in just 15 games with them to finish on a high note. However, that strong showing wasn’t enough to secure a roster spot to start the season. Florida had to go with only 21 players at the start of the year to remain cap-compliant and even his below-minimum AAV ($812.5K) wasn’t enough to save his spot. Instead, he cleared waivers in training camp and was assigned to the Checkers where he has two assists in five appearances so far. Blueliner Radko Gudas remains day-to-day with an undisclosed injury although the hope is that he’ll be good to go on Wednesday. With the team only carrying seven defenders and the minimum of 12 forwards, that left them with no spare players for tonight. Reinhardt’s addition changes that and with the team operating in LTIR at the moment, they could very well decide to keep Reinhardt around as injury insurance beyond just tonight’s game.

items.title: Kings Recall Taylor Ward, Assign Jared Wright To AHL
items.summary: The Los Angeles Kings have recalled winger Taylor Ward from AHL Ontario and assigned winger Jared Wright to the Reign.
items.body: Register Login Kings Recall Taylor Ward, Assign Jared Wright To AHL By Brian La Rose | at October 17, 2026 2:13 pm The Kings have made a pair of roster moves leading into tonight’s game against Boston. The team announced that they’ve recalled winger Taylor Ward from AHL Ontario and reassigned winger Jared Wright to the Reign. It’s the first recall of the season for Ward after he cleared waivers last month. The 28-year-old got into 36 games with Los Angeles last season, notching three goals and four assists in 9:28 per game of playing time. That was enough to secure him a two-year, one-way extension midseason worth $875K on average. Speculatively, the multi-year commitment at NHL money may have helped play a role in his passing through waivers in training camp. Ward is off to a solid start to his campaign with Ontario, collecting two goals and an assist in his first four outings. He also had a dozen goals in 32 appearances with the Reign last season. As for Wright, this is his second assignment to the minors this week alone. On his last one, he made one appearance against San Diego before being recalled to the Kings where he has largely served as a reserve forward in the early going. Signed to a two-year, one-way extension of his own earlier this month, Wright has three points in as many games with Ontario and has made one appearance with the Kings. It’s quite possible that this is another short-term assignment, allowing Wright to get a game in with Ontario tonight against Henderson, which would make him eligible to be recalled once again. This way, the Kings ensure that he’s still seeing at least somewhat regular game action despite being a frequent scratch early with the big club.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Toronto Maple Leafs got a tough update on one of their key players, as they announced on Saturday that center John Tavares is week-to-week with a lower-body injury. Tavares sustained the injury during Thursday’s 5-4 overtime loss to the Buffalo Sabres . Nick Paul and Josh Norris were tangled with each other in the middle of the ice, and when Paul shoved Norris onto the ice, Norris fell into a passing Tavares, taking the 36 year old’s legs out from underneath him and causing him to fall awkwardly on the ice. He remained on the ice for a bit before requiring assistance to the dressing room, and did not return to the game. According to reports from the Leafs’ media, the team also mentioned that Tavares’ week-to-week designation could keep him out of the lineup for anywhere between one to six weeks, which would potentially keep him out of the lineup until the end of November. Based on the provided timeline, Tavares is projected to miss anywhere between four and 19 games. At this point in time, the Leafs have not announced if Tavares has been placed on injured reserve or long-term injured reserve, nor have they announced any corresponding roster moves. One will likely be needed though, as the Leafs are down to only 12 forwards on their roster. The injury is a tough break for Tavares, who was continuing on his strong production even into late 30s with two goals and five assists for seven points in seven games before the injury. It also comes only two games after Tavares had missed a game to attend the birth of his child. With Tavares out, Easton Cowan moves up to the second line to play alongside Nick Paul and Kirill Marchenko, a combination which has only played 13 seconds together in passing this season.

items.title: Maple Leafs’ John Tavares out week-to-week with lower-body injury
items.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs are going to be without another key veteran moving forward. John Tavares will be sidelined week-to-week with a lower-body injury, the team announced Saturday. The designation means Tavares could miss up to six weeks, according to the team . Tavares exited early in the third period Thursday against the Buffalo Sabres after an awkward collision with Josh Norris. Norris collided with Tavares' lower body unexpectedly, and the Maple Leafs forward fell to the ice in discomfort. Tavares remained on the ice in visible pain before a trainer came out to assist him to the dressing room. Tavares has two goals and five assists through seven games on the season. He also missed a contest earlier this week due to the birth of his son. The 36-year-old has been mostly healthy through his Maple Leafs tenure. He's missed just 14 games total over the past five seasons and played in all 82 last season. Now, Tavares joins rugged blue-liner Chris Tanev on the Maple Leafs' injury report as they get set to face his former team, the New York Islanders, on Rogers Saturday Night Hockey (Sportsnet, Sportsnet+, 7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT). It's not yet apparent who will replace Tavares in the Maple Leafs lineup.

items.body: Fortunately for the Flyers, Philadelphia is known as a patient and understanding sports city. (If only there was a universal sarcasm font.) items.title: Meet trailblazer Onni Hautamaki, Finland’s first NHL official
items.summary: Onni Hautamaki is the latest trailblazer in NHL officiating: a rising star, the proof that if you’re good enough in hockey, they’ll find you anywhere. Sportsnet’s Frank Seravalli has the story on the league’s first Finnish official.
items.body: Unbeknownst to almost anyone inside Little Caesars Arena, chills coursed through the veins of linesperson Onni Hautamäki as he carved into the ice for the first time on Tuesday night. Yes, the solo rookie lap tradition extends to the officials’ ranks, too — and it just hits different when you’re the first Finnish official to make your NHL debut, on your 31st birthday no less. “It was unreal,” Hautamäki said in a phone interview on Wednesday. “It is an honour and a privilege to be the first Finn, I am very proud. It’s just unbelievable. To wear that NHL crest for the first time, to take that lap, it was a night that I’ll remember all my life.” For Hautamäki, Tuesday in Detroit was a night nearly 15 years in the making since he stopped playing junior hockey as a 16-year-old and picked up a whistle. IIHF director of officiating Scott Zelkin identified Hautamäki during a seven-year run rising through the ranks of Liiga, Finland’s top pro league, and he then burst onto the NHL’s radar at international events like the world juniors and world championship. After a five-game trial run in the AHL last year, NHL director of officiating scouting and development Al Kimmel worked with the IIHF to help nominate Hautamäki for the 2026 Olympics. Hautamäki worked the lines for five contests in Milan before being selected for a holy-grail assignment: the gold-medal game. items.title: Penguins’ Sidney Crosby passes Thornton for seventh in NHL all-time assists
items.summary: Sidney Crosby’s legend continues to grow, as he climbed up the NHL’s all-time assists list.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Sidney Crosby’s start to the 2026-27 season might not be as productive as hoped, but his legend continued to grow on Friday night, as he rose up the NHL’s all-time assist list. The Pittsburgh Penguins captain posted the 1,110th assist of his illustrious career against the Colorado Avalanche in a 5-2 loss. While the result didn’t fall Pittsburgh’s way, the point pushed Crosby past Joe Thornton on the league’s all-time assists list, into seventh place. Crosby now sits 25 assists behind Paul Coffey, whose 1,135 assists are good for sixth place, but well behind Wayne Gretzky’s lead of 1,963 assists, which remains more career assists than any other NHL player has points. In terms of points, Crosby is also approaching the top five, with his 1,766 only 32 short of fifth-place in all-time points, Ron Francis. At 39, Crosby’s impact has slightly diminished with the Penguins. Playing alongside Kris Letang and Evgeni Malkin in his 22nd season with the club, the trio has become the longest-serving trio in NHL history. However, Crosby has two goals and three assists for five points in eight games, while the Penguins have managed only three wins in those contests. Despite being in the twilight of his career, Crosby will look to return to at least a point-per-game pace in the near future. Last season, he netted 29 goals and 45 assists for 74 points in 68 games, missing time due to an injury sustained during Canada’s silver-medal run at the Milan Cortina 2026 Olympics. Through his entire 22-year career, he has never finished a season below a point-per-game total. items.body: DENVER — Nathan MacKinnon had three assists and a power-play goal, Artturi Lehkonen scored twice and the Colorado Avalanche rallied to beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 5-2 on Friday night. T.J. Hughes scored his first NHL goal, while Mackenzie Blackwood settled in after a shaky start to stop 29 shots. Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust gave Pittsburgh a 2-0 lead after scoring 29 seconds apart midway through the first period. The Avalanche erupted for five straight tallies, including three in the second period. Colorado finished one of four on the power play in the Avalanche debut of assistant coach Brett McLean. He's in charge of the unit after Dave Hakstol left to take over as head coach of the men's hockey program at Arizona State. Lehkonen's second goal tied it 25 seconds into the second period. Captain Gabriel Landeskog had a goal nearly four minutes later for his 83rd career go-ahead score. He's tied with Mikko Rantanen for sixth-most in Avalanche history. Hall of Famer Joe Sakic tops the list with 210. Hughes got free down low and poked in a pass from MacKinnon. He was hugged by Cale Makar and then playfully squirted with water by Landeskog as Hughes made his way past the bench. Sidney Crosby notched his 1,110th career assist to move into sole possession of seventh place in NHL history. He's also one assist shy of matching Ray Bourque (1,111 with Boston) for the most in league history with a one franchise. MacKinnon improved to 12-6-3 when playing against Crosby, his good buddy from Nova Scotia. MacKinnon was awarded a penalty shot, but was stopped by Arturs Silovs. Avalanche: Two-game road swing starting Monday night at Philadelphia.

items.title: Maple Leafs Place Miles Wood On IR
items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs have placed winger Miles Wood on injured reserve.
items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Place Miles Wood On IR By Brian La Rose | at October 16, 2026 8:00 pm The injury list has been pretty long already this season for the Maple Leafs, who find themselves down several regulars in the early going. Now, one of the players called up to cover for those injuries is injured himself without even playing one game. Per the NHL’s media site, winger Miles Wood has been placed on injured reserve. The 31-year-old cleared waivers back in training camp and was assigned to the minors but found himself on the move soon after as he was moved to Toronto as part of the Kirill Marchenko trade. His inclusion appeared to be more for salary cap purposes as he carries a $2.5MM cap charge for the next three years, a hefty price tag for someone to play in the AHL. He earned that money over a decade’s worth of games, where he has 99 goals and 97 assists in 567 appearances. Wood remained on assignment to the Marlies early in the season and hadn’t seen game action prior to his recall last week. He got into some practices and evidently sustained some sort of injury, although the nature is undisclosed and there’s no word on a timeline for his return. Toronto has a little under $5MM remaining in LTIR room, per PuckPedia . That pool will be reduced by $3.25MM in the coming days with Dakota Joshua ’s pending return but even so, they can easily afford to carry Wood on IR for the time being. If Wood is eventually deemed to miss at least 10 games and 24 days, he’ll be eligible to be transferred to LTIR himself. The Maple Leafs now have one open spot on their active roster, though that could be given to Joshua over the next few days.

Florida Panthers forward Brady Tkachuk , the 65th and newest player on the list, is bidding to become the first to make it three in a row -- a hat trick of hat tricks. Eight times, since Denneny with the Ottawa Senators in 1917 through Teemu Selanne with the Winnipeg Jets in 1993, a player has had consecutive hat tricks and then scored twice in a third game, coming one goal short of the three-peat. Others on the close-but-no-cigar list: Alexander Mogilny , Buffalo Sabres, 1992-93; Wayne Gretzky , Edmonton Oilers, 1984; Phil Esposito , Boston Bruins, 1974; Claude Larose, Montreal Canadiens, 1974; Punch Broadbent , Senators, 1922; and Malone, Hamilton Tigers, 1921. items.body: Allowing third-most goals-against in NHL entering game against Rangers Saturday Rick Bowness said everyone associated with the Columbus Blue Jackets "should be very angry with where we are." The coach, speaking on Friday, said he especially was bothered by the fact that the Blue Jackets have allowed an average of 4.20 goals per game, tied for the third most in the NHL. "We're 30th in the League in goals-against -- 30th," Bowness said. "I've never coached a team that was 30th in the League in goals-against." The Blue Jackets (2-3-0), who host the New York Rangers at Nationwide Arena on Saturday (7 p.m. ET; CBJHN, CBJNHL, MSG), haven't played since Tuesday, a 7-3 home loss to the Florida Panthers. That followed a 5-3 loss at the St. Louis Blues on Saturday. They have allowed at least three goals in four of their five games and are 1-3-0 after a 6-3 win against the Buffalo Sabres in their season opener Oct. 1. After the loss to the Panthers, Bowness voiced his frustration with his team. "We beat ourselves in St. Louis. We beat ourselves tonight," Bowness said. "So you have to hope, you've got to believe, that that performance tonight will embarrass them enough to stop this, right? Because if they're not embarrassed by that, we don't want them on the team. It's as simple as that. "I'm not a babysitter. I'm too old to be a babysitter for these guys. You're a professional athlete, prepare yourself to play properly." This is not the first time that Bowness has called out his team. Last season, after the Blue Jackets had been eliminated from Stanley Cup Playoff contention, Bowness said if he returned to Columbus this season, he would be "changing the culture." items.title: Why are teams struggling to sell out games?
items.summary: The Vegas Golden Knights snapped a nine-year sellout streak this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images The NHL is a gate-driven league. You may have heard this said a time or two before. While leagues like the NFL and NBA generate a major portion of their revenue from broadcasting deals, the NHL still relies much more heavily on in-person attendance. It can’t be a great sign, then, that teams around the league have been failing to sell out early in the season. The Vegas Golden Knights snapped their nine-year sellout streak on October 8, when they hit just 92% attendance for a game against the Toronto Maple Leafs . On Thursday, the Edmonton Oilers had over 2,000 empty seats for their home game against the Utah Mammoth . Multiple other teams have seen their attendance fall short of expectations. On Friday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , hosts Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton discussed the possible reasons for the disappointing attendance figures across the NHL. items.title: Ducks’ rebuild provides blueprint for Flames to follow
items.summary: As the Flames embark on their own rebuild, the Ducks are beginning to look an awful lot like the blueprint GM Craig Conroy would love to follow, writes Eric Francis.
items.body: That was the timeline Pat Verbeek had in mind shortly after he took the wheel in Anaheim, a franchise that needed to tear things down before it could dream of building something special again. The goal wasn't to win a Stanley Cup in five years. It wasn't even to guarantee a playoff spot. It was to become a team that could start contending for a sprinkling of spring hockey. As the Calgary Flames embark on their own uncomfortable transition, Verbeek's Anaheim Ducks are beginning to look an awful lot like the blueprint Craig Conroy would love to follow. The similarities aren't lost on Verbeek, who has watched his young Ducks take a significant step forward after years of accumulating draft picks, developing talent and carefully adding veterans to help the kids grow. "When I talk to Connie, yeah," Verbeek said of the parallels between Anaheim's rebuild and Calgary's. "Transitioning is probably the hardest thing to do, not wanting to take a step back, but just kind of gaining a little ground every year.” In a one-on-one chat outside the Ducks dressing room, Verbeek said that when he arrived in Anaheim in Feb. 2022, his first instinct was to try to retain the veteran foundation on a team that missed the playoffs three years running. But Josh Manson, Hampus Lindholm and Rickard Rakell couldn't be signed to new deals, forcing the general manager to change course. That pivot, as he calls it, became the foundation of the rebuild. Rather than cling to a group that wasn't going to take the Ducks where they wanted to go, Verbeek traded those veterans and began stockpiling draft picks, putting an emphasis on identifying and developing young talent. items.body: Register Login Seattle Kraken Recall Ty Nelson By Brennan McClain | at October 16, 2026 1:00 pm The Seattle Kraken have recalled defensive reinforcements after Brandon Montour suffered a lower-body injury last night. According to a team announcement , the Kraken recalled defenseman Ty Nelson from the AHL’s Coachella Valley Firebirds. Nelson has continued his strong two-way play in the AHL. Since debuting with AHL Coachella Valley in 2024-25, he has registered 17 goals and 71 points in 140 games with a +34 rating. He has puck-moving skills similar to those of other smaller defensemen. Still, despite standing at 5’10″and weighing 198 lbs, Nelson plays extremely large. They aren’t all bone-crushing hits, but he plays with an extremely high motor and sacrifices his body almost every shift. Unfortunately, despite his strong play with the Firebirds, Nelson hasn’t made his NHL debut. Depending on the severity of Montour’s injury, that could change during his current recall. items.title: ‘Should all be very angry’: Cooler heads not prevailing for Blue Jackets’ Bowness
items.body: The Columbus Blue Jackets coach continued his public tirade over his team's defence on Friday three days after it suffered a 7-3 loss to the Floridaa Panthers. "Right now, we should all be very angry at where we are," Bowness told reporters . "You look at our team. We’re 30th in the league in goals against. I’ve never coached a team that was 30th in the league in goals against … I’m mad. I keep seeing 30th goals against. That bothers me." Columbus, which sits 3-2 on the season, is tied with the Los Angeles Kings for third-last in the NHL at 4.20 goals against per game. The Blue Jackets fell apart in the second period of the Panthers loss, allowing four goals including a natural hat trick from Brady Tkachuk. Forward Mathieu Olivier did his team no favours either, taking an ill-advised five-minute major penalty for slashing, which led to his subsequent ejection and another goal against. "Yeah. They’re like I am. They’re not happy where they are," he said. The 71-year-old coach ripped into his players in the immediate aftermath of the game on Tuesday, calling the performance "embarrassing." "You gotta believe that performance will embarrass them enough to stop this, right?" Bowness told reporters . "Because if they're not embarrassed by that, we don't want them on the team. Simple as that." "I know it looks bad, but I believe in what we're doing. I believe in them. I believe we can fix the problems," the bench boss added. "That all being said, if (the game) doesn't get their attention, then they're on the wrong team." items.body: Register Login Midday Notes: Raddysh, Back, Xhekaj By Marcus Antonelli | at October 16, 2026 11:26 am The New York Rangers have recalled Taylor Raddysh from Hartford, their AHL affiliate, and have sent down Jaroslav Chmelar . Raddysh joins the team having played the start of his 2026-27 campaign with three goals for five points in five AHL contests. The former second-round pick is in the second year of a two-year, $1.5MM AAV contract. At age 28, Raddysh has solidified his professional profile as a depth piece for an organization that can provide some worthy second-hand offense. In his first year with New York, he scored 19 points in 68 games. Historically, Raddysh has seen a near 40-point campaign with the Blackhawks back in 2022-23. Even then, penalty killing and defensive prowess are valuable things the Rangers will need out of him, which he has been prominent in. Chmelar, in comparison, has been averaging less NHL time than what Raddysh usually provides in a similar role. The former fifth-round pick out of Czechia has started his first seven NHL games in 2026-27 with around eight minutes of ice time at 5-on-5 and has yet to produce a point. The 23-year-old has fared better in the AHL, having scored 56 points across three seasons, totaling 124 games. He could benefit from more minutes, similar to how Cole Beaudoin wouldn’t receive quality NHL ice time yet. He’s known as a forward who attacks straight with his speed, but has areas to improve in his handling, which, if mastered, could help with more offensive opportunities.

items.body: The Montreal Canadiens will be without the younger Xhekaj for a little while. Florian Xhekaj will be out for two weeks with a lower-body injury, the team shared on Friday. The winger missed the home game against the Red Wings on Saturday with an undisclosed injury and also sat out the back-to-backs on Tuesday and Wednesday. On Monday, Xhekaj appeared to be in lower-body pain at practice and left the ice early. The 22-year-old fourth-round pick has appeared in two games for the Canadiens this season while logging no points and averaging 7:36 minutes on the ice. The team also shared on Friday that there is no change to Matheson's status and he remains day-to-day with a lower-body injury. Perron, who had been an unrestricted free agent since July 1, will be playing in his 20th NHL season. "We are excited to welcome David and his family to the Stars organization," Stars general manager Jim Nill said. "He brings a competitive mindset and a proven ability to perform in big moments. We believe his veteran leadership and skill set will be a valuable addition to our group as we continue to build toward our goal of winning a Stanley Cup." The Stars (3-3-1) are currently without forward Matt Duchene for three months because of core muscle surgery. With his unmistakable voice, colorful vocabulary, and extraordinary gift for describing the action as it unfolded, Emrick provided the soundtrack to some of the most memorable moments in NHL history. Protecting a one-goal lead late in the third period, Washington appeared to be in serious trouble when Vegas forward Alex Tuch found himself staring at a seemingly wide-open net. But Holtby lunged across his crease with his stick and somehow kept the puck out, making arguably the greatest save in Stanley Cup Final history. “Oh, and it didn’t go!” Emrick exclaimed in disbelief. “It was Tuch with the wide-open net!” It was vintage Emrick: spontaneous, emotional, and perfectly capturing the disbelief of everyone watching. items.body: Actor, survivor joins cause that has become ‘personal’ for team DETROIT -- Dave Coulier stood outside the Detroit Red Wings dressing room Thursday, hanging out with fellow “Full House” star Andrea Barber. The 67-year-old actor had come to Little Caesars Arena for two reasons: One, he grew up a huge Red Wings fan in St. Clair Shores, Michigan. Two, Detroit was hosting Hockey Fights Cancer Night. Coulier is a cancer survivor. He and Barber wore special Red Wings Hockey Fights Cancer jerseys to a game against the Philadelphia Flyers, raising awareness and money for the cause. “Early screenings saved my life twice now with Non-Hodgkin lymphoma and carcinoma,” Coulier said. “It makes a big difference. It’s not sexy, but get that prostate exam, get that colonoscopy, get those mammograms. I’m encouraging people to do so.” Hockey Fights Cancer, a joint initiative of the NHL and NHL Players’ Association, is in its 28th season and has generated more than $53 million in total fundraising. Since partnering with the V Foundation in 2023, it has raised more than $12.3 million for cancer research and awarded 42 research grants. This night was particularly meaningful for the Red Wings. Jenny Baumann, the wife of physical therapist and assistant athletic trainer Russ Baumann, passed away due to cancer Saturday. She was 55. Red Wings coach Todd McLellan choked up as he talked about it. This past weekend we lost Jenny Baumann. Jenny is the wife of Physical Therapist and Assistant Athletic Trainer, Russ Baumann. items.body: We’re still less than three weeks into the 2026-27 campaign and it’s easy to jump to conclusions about things that may turn out to be silly a month from now. Still, it’s fun to look around the league at some anomalies and ponder if they could become trends. Maybe a team that was destined to be a basement dweller catches fire in the first half-dozen games and is sitting near the top of its division. Or there might be a player that never really had a nose for the net who is suddenly shooting the lights out. What about the goalie that struggled mightily last year who is all of a sudden unbeatable? History tells many of these things won’t hold up for 80-plus games, but it doesn’t make them any less eye-popping for now. There’s also the odd early-season trend that turns out to have legs and be sustainable. The Pittsburgh Penguins from a year ago are a good example: after missing the playoffs for three straight seasons, the Pens won six of their first eight games and no one thought it would last. However, five months later, Pittsburgh claimed a playoff spot and never really slowed down. items.body: LAS VEGAS — Mark Stone had the fourth hat trick of his career and the Vegas Golden Knights beat the Calgary Flames 6-2 on Thursday night. items.body: LAS VEGAS — Rasmus Andersson knows what Calgary Flames fans are going through right now. He spent nine years with the organization, arriving as a 21-year-old and leaving as a 29-year-old. He built a family in Calgary and experienced the highs and lows of playing in a market where hockey means an awful lot to people. So when he sees his former team struggling through the earliest stages of a rebuild, he understands the frustration. He also knows there's a bigger picture at play. “You never want to see your old team struggle, right?” said the Vegas defender. “But at the same time, they went out and said it's a rebuild, and this is what the fans asked for.” It's a difficult balance for everyone involved. Fans want to see progress, young players need time to develop, and management is trying to build a team capable of competing for years to come. This will take time. Lots of it. Andersson's point isn't that Calgary supporters shouldn't be frustrated. It's that rebuilding is rarely a straight line, and patience becomes particularly important when there are growing pains, like the team’s 1-6 start, arrive. “They can't get impatient,” said Andersson, who has long monitored the pulse of the fans closer than most. “I don't read about it the same way as I did, but it still pops up here and there — I still see some comments like, ‘fire the coach, do this, do this.’ “Did guys think you could win seven in a row to start the season when you guys go out and say you want to rebuild? Some teams may indeed limit their mandated extra goalie to those in-case-of-emergency-break-glass situations where a last-minute or in-game injury or illness makes it impossible to call up a minor league goalie fast enough to fill in for a game. Lund is generally a well-regarded prospect, although he is not typically counted among the best in what is a deep Sharks farm system. items.body: CHICAGO — Chicago Blackhawks forward Patrick Kane earned another career milestone in becoming the NHL’s career leader in assists among U.S.-born players. The 37-year-old from Buffalo, New York, earned his 895th career assist on Connor Bedard’s game-opening power-play goal against the Winnipeg Jets on Thursday night. In doing so in his 1,377th game, Kane surpassed the American-born record held by defenseman Phil Housley, who had 894 assists in 1,496 games. Kane then added a second assist by having a hand in Artyom Levshunov's goal 1:37 into overtime of a 4-3 win. In January while with the Detroit Red Wings, Kane set the record for most points among American NHLers, with the two assists now increasing his total to 1,405. Kane is in his 20th NHL season and signed a two-year contract in July to return to Chicago where he won three Stanley Cups during his first 16 NHL seasons. items.summary: Montour had no goals and five assists in seven games prior to Thursday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images The Seattle Kraken could be looking at life without their most relied upon blueliner. Kraken defenseman Brandon Montour suffered a lower-body injury during Thursday’s road game against the Tampa Bay Lightning . The team has confirmed that he will not return to the game. It’s not exactly clear how Montour picked up the injury, but it may have occured during his last shift early in the second period when he was tripped up by Lightning forward Nikita Kucherov, causing him to fall somewhat awkwardly. Montour, 32, has no goals and five assists in seven games this season. He is also leading Seattle with a tick over 24 and half minutes of ice time per game. Last season, he notched 11 goals and 21 assists for 32 points in 64 games for Seattle, while leading the team in average ice time with about 22 and a half minutes. The Brantford, Ontario native is in his third season with the Kraken after signing with them on a seven-year, $50 million deal as an unrestricted free agent in July of 2024. Selected by the Anaheim Ducks in the second round of the 2014 NHL Entry Draft, Montour spent his first two plus NHL seasons in Anaheim before getting traded to the Buffalo Sabres at the 2019 deadline in exchange for defenseman Brendan Guhle and a first-round pick. After just 112 games for Buffalo spread over three seasons, he was traded to the Florida Panthers at the 2021 deadline for a third-round pick. Montour peaked in Florida, having his career-best campaign in 2022-23 with 16 goals and 57 assists for 73 points in 80 games, and helping the Panthers win the Stanley Cup in 2024 before departing for Seattle. After Thursday’s game in Tampa, the Kraken will finish up a five-game road trip against the Panthers on Saturday.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images A journeyman has found a new home in the Lone Star State. The Dallas Stars announced on Friday that they have signed forward David Perron to a one-year contract. The deal carries a prorated cap hit of $850,000 for the 2026-27 season. Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman was the first to report the signing. When the new season began, the 38-year-old remained unsigned . However, in the opening weeks of the campaign, the Stars realized they could utilize the tools the 20-year NHLer possesses. Perron moves to Dallas hoping to produce a little bit more and stay healthier than he has in the past couple of seasons. After an impressive stretch in which he posted at least 45 points eight years in a row, the Stanley Cup champion posted only 16 points in 43 games with the Ottawa Senators in 2024-25, improving only slightly to 28 points in 65 appearances last year. He started last season with the Sens before the trade deadline , when he was traded to the Detroit Red Wings , though he did little to better the Original Six team’s postseason chances, scoring just three goals in 16 contests. The Sherbrooke, Que. native has made his way around the NHL over his long career. After starting off with the St. Louis Blues , the team that took him in the first round of the 2007 NHL Draft, he was traded to the Edmonton Oilers in the summer of 2013. He was then dealt to the Pittsburgh Penguins in the middle of the 20214-15 campaign, but was on the move the following season, as he was traded to the Anaheim Ducks . He rejoined the Blues as a free agent in July 2016, but the Vegas Golden Knights claimed him in the expansion draft a year later. After one season in Sin City, he returned to the Blues and helped the franchise win its first Cup.

items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Ottawa’s Drake Batherson preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to Stephen Halliday’s goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 8:10 (11:50 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images The Toronto Maple Leafs announced Thursday that they have acquired forward Aatu Räty from the Vancouver Canucks in exchange for forwards Jacob Quillan and Brandon Buhr. Räty, 23, cleared waivers earlier on Thursday and will now be eligible to go between the NHL and AHL freely until he appears in 10 NHL games or spends 30 days on an NHL roster. The 6’2″ center has one goal in four games with the Canucks this season. The New York Islanders originally selected Räty in the second round (No. 52 overall) of the 2021 NHL Draft. The Oulu, Finland product spent the bulk of the 2025-26 season with the Canucks, collecting four goals and 14 points in 66 games while recording a 60.5 faceoff win percentage. Quillan, 24, is the main piece heading to Vancouver in the trade. The 6’1″ center split the 2025-26 regular season between the Maple Leafs and the AHL’s Toronto Marlies and ultimately won the 2026 Calder Cup as a member of the Marlies after scoring nine points in 19 playoff games. Buhr, also 24, signed with the Maple Leafs organization in March as an NCAA free agent from Union College. After scoring 19 goals and 36 points in 35 games as a senior at Union, the 6’2″ forward collected two assists in five games with the Marlies to conclude the 2025-26 regular season. Quillan and Buhr are both undrafted forwards who will provide additional organizational depth for the Canucks going forward. items.body: Register Login Vancouver Canucks Activate Filip Chytil By Brennan McClain | at October 15, 2026 5:48 pm As expected, the Vancouver Canucks announced they’ve activated center Filip Chytil from injured reserve. The oft-injured forward began the season on Vancouver’s injured reserve due to a shoulder injury. The news comes only a few minutes after the Canucks traded center Aatu Räty to the Toronto Maple Leafs, creating a roster spot for Chytil. Chytil, 27, was acquired from the New York Rangers in the trade that sent J.T. Miller eastbound in 2025. Chytil was considered a risky acquisition, having played only 10 games the previous season. Still, he was relatively healthy leading up to the trade, scoring 11 goals and 20 points in 41 contests with a +4 rating. Unfortunately, despite being rostered on the Canucks since January 2025, Chytil has appeared in only 27 games. A few months after Vancouver acquired him, Chytil received a high hit from Jason Dickinson , who was then with the Chicago Blackhawks, which prematurely ended his 2025-26 season due to a concussion. Chytil started the 2025-26 season healthy, but that didn’t last long. Chytil suffered another concussion six games into the season, sidelining him until late January. He appeared in another six games for the Canucks before chronic migraine conditions took him out of action for another two weeks. In a twisted turn of luck, as he was recovering from his migraines, Chytil was struck in the face by a puck at practice, ending his campaign due to a facial fracture. Fortunately, although he began the season on the injured reserve, at least it had nothing to do with his head.
